definition: An atom, molecule or ion with at least one unpaired electron, shown by a dot as in $\ce{Cl\bullet}$; most radicals are highly reactive.
Breaking a covalent bond so that each atom keeps one of the two bonding electrons, which forms two radicals.
A radical reaction in which each propagation step uses up one radical and makes another, so the cycle repeats between initiation and termination.
A reaction in which one atom or group in a molecule is replaced by another, such as a hydrogen atom of an alkane by a halogen atom.
